output.reason: Diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot wound now showing surrounding redness, swelling and tenderness — a possible diabetic foot infection that needs hands-on wound inspection (probing for depth/abscess, assessment of drainage, warmth, spread and perfusion) today; messaging cannot examine or probe the wound.
output.patientMessage: I recommend you be seen in person today — urgent care, your usual clinic, or a foot/wound service — for an infected-looking foot wound. In diabetes, a cut with surrounding redness, swelling and tenderness needs a hands-on wound exam that messaging can't replace. A Counsel clinician can stay involved in this thread. Go to an emergency department now if you develop fever, chills, spreading redness or red streaking, rapidly worsening pain, drainage, or the skin turns dusky or black.
differential: Wound-related cellulitis of the foot in a diabetic patient
Deeper diabetic foot infection or abscess, possibly involving underlying tissue
Local wound inflammation without established infection
